evidence.claim: Quanta reported record electric segment backlog at year-end 2025, supporting its role as the reference public benchmark for grid-services execution capacity.

evidence.claim: Quanta's current market capitalization was approximately $110.2 billion as of the June 16, 2026 finance snapshot, placing it in the mega-cap reference lane rather than the underfollowed discovery lane.

memory_update.text: For epc_grid_services, keep PWR as the reference benchmark only; avoid letting it crowd out smaller public contractors and upstream hardware suppliers.
MYRG is a direct underfollowed candidate for specialty electrical contracting exposure to utility T&D, substations, clean-energy interconnection, and grid construction capacity.
PRIM is a direct underfollowed candidate with large Utilities backlog, but later layers must separate electric-grid exposure from gas, pipeline, communications, and generalized infrastructure work.

PLPC should be tracked as a second-order upstream transmission hardware supplier; contractor backlog may be a leading demand signal for its energy-market sales, but this remains a hypothesis needing customer/product verification.

Layer 2 should verify customer/supplier links among utility capex plans, contractor backlogs, and upstream procurement for line hardware, conductor, poles, substation components, transformers, and protection equipment.

node: EPC, construction, and grid services contractors
summary: Expanded the EPC/grid-services node using a two-lane funnel. Quanta Services is retained as the high-attention reference benchmark because its electric backlog validates demand for grid execution capacity. The underfollowed lane adds MYR Group and Primoris as smaller public contractors with direct utility/transmission/construction exposure, plus Preformed Line Products as a second-order upstream hardware supplier whose demand may precede contractor field deployment. The key Serenity angle is that labor, permitting, and project-execution scarcity may shift value not only to prime contractors but also to specialized electrical contractors and hardware vendors embedded in utility transmission and distribution work.
